values.event_label: 'Clarify rules inclusion and failure rules' (ethereum/EIPs#4757). Rule 1 changes from "the transaction is valid, may be included in a block and aborts exceptionally" to "the transaction is invalid"; rule 2 states the initcode cost is part of the intrinsic gas cost; rule 3 changes CREATE and CREATE2 oversize behaviour from exceptional abort to pushing 0 on the stack; the "How to report initcode limit violation?" rationale is rewritten accordingly; two test cases about intrinsic-gas coverage are added; Andrei Maiboroda is added as an author.
values.rationale: Reverses the block-inclusion semantics of oversize create transactions and the failure mode of the creation instructions, both of which change consensus behaviour and the tests required for it.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit d38a4add0cfd: EIP-3860: Clarify rules inclusion and failure rules (#4757)

values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit 9e393a79d993: Force usage of included LICENSE file (#5055)

values.event_label: 'Clarify gas deduction in failure cases' (ethereum/EIPs#5130). Rule 3 gains the sentence "Gas for initcode execution is not deducted in this case."; rule 2's trailing note is turned into an italic aside.
values.rationale: Specifies gas accounting when the initcode length check fails, a consensus-relevant detail that implementations and tests must reproduce. Continues the rule-3 failure-semantics thread started in eip3860-e02.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit d59cf1a7c7d4: EIP-3860: Clarify gas deduction in failure cases (#5130)

values.event_label: 'Clarify nonce rules' (ethereum/EIPs#6040). Rule 3 gains "and caller's nonce is not incremented"; rule 4 gains "If the instruction fails due to the initcode length check of point 3, this cost is not deducted."; the Security Considerations section is moved after Test Cases; the EIP-3670 mention becomes a markdown link; the go-ethereum release link and some prose are reflowed; the 'requires' frontmatter line moves below 'created'.
values.rationale: Nonce handling and the non-deduction of the word cost on failure are observable consensus effects; the remaining edits in the same commit are formatting.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit 7fa3a41afeb4: Update EIP-3860: Clarify nonce rules (#6040)

values.event_label: 'Change the failure to OOG' (ethereum/EIPs#6249). Rule 3 reverts to an exceptional abort "(as if it runs out of gas)" instead of pushing 0 on the stack, rule 4 drops the conditional non-deduction sentence added in eip3860-e05, and the violation-reporting rationale is rewritten around the ordering of early out-of-gas checks.
values.rationale: Final change to the failure semantics of oversize initcode in CREATE and CREATE2, undoing the model introduced in eip3860-e02 and refined in eip3860-e04 and eip3860-e05. This is the state shipped in Shanghai and the state at the pin.
values.source_title: ethereum/EIPs commit b0ace5758c49: EIP-3860: Change the failure to OOG (#6249)

values.rationale: Classified as a dependency change because it removes an explicit cross-EIP reference, but non_substantive: EIP-3670 appeared only in the Motivation as an example of a future proposal that would benefit from the cost system, and its removal changes no rule, parameter or interface. The status edit is process metadata.

values.event_label: Specifies the serialisation position of the new fields: block body becomes RLP([transactions, ommers, withdrawals]) and block RLP becomes RLP([header, transactions, ommers, withdrawals]); adds a dedicated 'New field in the execution block header: withdrawals root' section with the full 16-element header RLP list ending in `withdrawals_root`; adds two NOTEs referring to EIP-3675 for the fixed ommers value and other fixed header values; drops the TODO about logs and receipts; expands the rationale on operations vs transactions and on the block-footprint bound (~1% of average block size).
values.rationale: Defines the concrete block-body and block-header encodings that clients must implement, and removes an unresolved specification TODO.

values.rationale: Changes the wire encoding of every withdrawal and therefore the withdrawals_root computation; a consensus-relevant serialisation change.

values.event_label: Editing pass (PR #5697) that re-frames the whole specification from 'block' to 'execution payload' terminology and corrects the header RLP illustration: the fixed ommers hash constant, difficulty 0 and the zero nonce are inlined, `bloom`/`time`/`mix_hash` are renamed to `logs_bloom`/`timestamp`/`prev_randao`, and the previously missing `base_fee_per_gas` field is added before `withdrawals_root`; the 'Commitment to withdrawals' and 'New field in the header' sections are merged; the note now cites EIP-3675 and EIP-4399; state-transition wording changes from 'should increase' to 'increases'; the `index` is described as uniquely identifying each withdrawal.
values.rationale: Corrects the illustrated header field list (adding base_fee_per_gas) and firms up normative wording; the header layout is consensus-critical.

values.event_label: Adds a fourth field to the Withdrawal object: the consensus-layer `validator_index`. The schema becomes `[index, validator_index, address, amount]`, examples are updated, and the `index` is documented as a global counter starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 per withdrawal. Also introduces the 'compuggational' typo in the rationale.
values.rationale: Adds a field to the serialised withdrawal structure and pins down index semantics.

values.event_label: Frontmatter reclassification only - 'type: Standards Track' plus 'category: Core' is replaced by 'type: Meta'. No body text changed.
values.rationale: Recorded as substantive because the Standards Track/Core to Meta reclassification changes the document's normative standing in the EIP process - it is the field that tells client teams whether the proposal is a protocol change requiring implementation. This is the classification the Shanghai fork record later relies on when distinguishing EIP-6049 from the fork's core protocol changes. change_type is clarification rather than normative_behavior because no specification text was altered; the change makes explicit what the creation text already implied ('No changes to clients is applicable'). Confidence is medium: a narrower reading would treat a frontmatter-only edit as editorial metadata. The merging pull request (#6064) carries only the repository's PR-template boilerplate, so no author rationale is on record (gh-pr-6064).
